official.deadline_note: Published 2026-cycle wording: 'The application should be submitted by September 25, 2026' and 'Last date for submission of the application is September 25, 2026.' That date has passed; applications are invited annually through announcements in Indian national newspapers and the notification on the ICAR website, with Indian diplomatic missions informed by e-mail. No 2027-cycle date has been published yet.
official.application_cycle: 2026 cycle; applications invited on an annual basis
official.status_note: The 2026 cycle's last date (September 25, 2026) has passed. The fellowship page and notification remain live, and the guidelines state applications are invited every year, so a fresh call is expected; the 2026 call PDF (uploaded August 2026) is still the current published scheme document.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Guideline 14 'Payment of Fee': 'All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled will be paid by the fellow himself out of the fellowship grant or from his/ her own resources.' Tuition/fees are NOT covered.
benefits: Thirty (30) fellowships for a duration of three years available every year
Indian fellows going abroad: US$ 2,000/- per month plus lump-sum contingent and preparatory expenses of US$ 1,000/- per year
Overseas fellows in India: INR 40,000/- per month plus lump-sum contingent and preparatory expenses of INR 25,000/- per year
To-and-fro economy class international air ticket by the shortest route, provided by the Council, for both Indian and overseas candidates
Overseas fellows additionally get economy-class travel cost reimbursement from port of arrival in India to the destination university and back
In-service fellows may continue to receive salary, leave and benefits from the parent organization during the tenure
eligibility: Master's degree in agriculture/allied sciences with Overall Grade Point Average (OGPA) 6.60 out of 10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent
Fresh candidates not more than 35 years of age, and in-service candidates up to 40 years, on the last date prescribed for receipt of applications
Fresh candidates must have completed the qualifying Master's degree not more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission
In-service Indian candidates must be employed in the ICAR-AU system
Open to Indian nationals (study abroad at identified overseas universities/institutions) and overseas nationals (study at Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system)
Clear record of good conduct throughout, certified by the Competent Authority of the university last attended or the present employer
requirements: The area of study and proposed research must fall in the identified priority areas relevant to Indian/global agriculture, notified by the Council one year in advance
Applicants must obtain acceptance of admission to the PhD programme at their own level; the acceptance letter should preferably be enclosed with the application and must be furnished at interview
Two references with contact e-mail addresses who may be contacted directly by the Council (one preferably the current supervisor, one an expert in the area)
Selected candidates must register for the programme within one year of the fellowship award letter, failing which the offer is terminated automatically

Indian fellows going abroad must furnish an irrevocable bank guarantee of US$ 10,000/- (rupee equivalent) in favour of the Secretary, ICAR, valid till completion; overseas fellows have Rs. 2,00,000 recovered in two installments from the fellowship grant
Indian fellows must return to India after completing the PhD; in-service Indian fellows execute a bond to serve the deputing institution for at least three years
documents: Completed NS-ICAR IF application proforma with recent photograph and passport/Aadhaar details
Copies of degrees, mark sheets and academic records from the graduate degree onwards
Copy of the proposed research plan and title of proposed research
Letter of acceptance for admission from the host university
Two referee comments in the prescribed format (one preferably the applicant's supervisor)
Certificate of good conduct from the Competent Authority of the university last attended or present employer
Deputation approval from the Director of the ICAR institute or Vice-Chancellor, for in-service Indian candidates
Certificate of physical fitness by an authorized Medical Doctor
For overseas applicants: Certificate of Proficiency in English and Certificate of the Indian Diplomatic Representative certifying domicile and verified entries
selection_criteria: Evaluation on a weighted scale taking into account relevance of the area of study, proposed research plan, academic records, achievements and past work experience
Subsequent interview by a Selection Committee constituted by the Council, empowered to judge suitability regarding the importance of the area of study and research plan
The Committee may conduct telephonic/teleconferencing interviews; overseas candidates may be interviewed by Council-identified experts based in their home country
At interview the applicant must furnish the letter of acceptance for admission from the host university
coverage: Monthly fellowship stipend: US$ 2,000 per month for Indian fellows abroad, INR 40,000 per month for overseas fellows in India
Annual lump-sum contingent and preparatory expenses: up to US$ 1,000 per year (Indian fellows abroad) or INR 25,000 per year (overseas fellows in India)
To-and-fro economy class international air travel by the shortest route, air tickets provided by the Council
Economy-class travel reimbursement within India from port of arrival to host university and back, for overseas fellows

Not covered: host institution fees, medical insurance and other costs, which the fellow meets from the fellowship or own resources; domestic Indian travel of Indian fellows is borne by the fellow or sponsoring organisation
application_method: Applications are invited annually through announcements in Indian national newspapers and the notification on the ICAR website, with Indian diplomatic missions informed by e-mail
Complete the prescribed application proforma available on the ICAR website
Submit the application by e-mail to ADG (HRD) at adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the subject line 'Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number'
Send the complete application with enclosures on or before the last date (September 25, 2026 for the 2026 cycle)
official.application_route: Respond to the annual ICAR call by e-mailing the completed prescribed proforma with all certified enclosures to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com using the prescribed subject line.
official.study_mode: Full-time; the fellow must devote full time to the chosen area of study/research during the tenure
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Indian and overseas nationals; overseas applicants must certify permanent domicile through the Indian Diplomatic Representative
official.international_eligibility: Yes, by design: overseas nationals study at Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system and Indian nationals study at identified overseas universities/institutions
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Doctoral study must be in agriculture and allied sciences within the ICAR-notified priority areas; the host must be an identified overseas institution (Indian applicants) or an identified Indian AU in the ICAR-AU system (overseas applicants)
official.research_requirement: A copy of the proposed research plan must be enclosed with the application and the title of the proposed research plan is a mandatory field of the proforma; the area of study must match a notified priority area
official.duration: Three years; tenure will not be extended in so far as Council support is concerned
official.description: ICAR instituted International Fellowships with the dual purpose of human resource development in cutting-edge technologies and demonstrating the strength of the Indian agricultural system abroad, training Indian candidates in the best laboratories worldwide and exposing overseas candidates to the best Indian Agricultural Universities, to create a pool of scientist-envoys for enhanced future cooperation.
official.program_type: International doctoral research fellowship in agriculture and allied sciences
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL score is prescribed. The proforma self-rates written and spoken English as Good/Fair/Poor, and overseas applicants must furnish a Certificate of Proficiency in English bearing the seal of the Indian Diplomatic Mission.

not_confirmed: No IELTS/TOEFL minimum score exists in the guidelines
No institutional deadline separate from the programme deadline is published
No 2027-cycle deadline has been announced yet
The on-line submission wording in guideline 8.1 is not tied to a named portal in the 2026 call, which routes applications by e-mail
Host university fee levels, which vary by institution, are not published by ICAR

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 30-seat, three-year doctoral fellowship that runs in both directions: Indian Master's graduates study abroad at ICAR-listed universities on US$2,000 a month plus up to US$1,000 a year in contingency, while overseas nationals pursue a PhD at an Indian agricultural university on INR 40,000 a month plus INR 25,000 a year. ICAR pays return economy air travel and can help with intra-India travel for overseas fellows, but the host university's fees, medical insurance and your own domestic travel remain your expense. The call surfaces once a year with an end-September deadline in recent cycles, and the file is unusually certificate-heavy, so secure your host admission and signatures months before the window opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent or in-service Master's graduates in agriculture and allied sciences (OGPA 6.60/10 or 65%+) aged under 35 (under 40 if in-service) who can win a PhD seat at an ICAR-listed institution in a notified priority area.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a host PhD admission or at least initiate correspondence early: the acceptance letter should ideally accompany the application and must be produced at the interview
Match your proposed research to the exact wording of ICAR's notified priority areas and name the host institution from the published lists
Line up two referees with working e-mail addresses (one preferably your current supervisor) and brief them on the prescribed referee format
Request the good-conduct certificate from the university last attended, and deputation approval from your ICAR institute/AU Vice-Chancellor if you are in-service
Prepare your publications list in the proforma's format (authors, title, journal name, NAAS journal ID and NAAS score, with copies attached)

Keep passport/Aadhaar details, a recent photograph and a doctor-signed physical fitness certificate ready; overseas applicants additionally need the Indian Diplomatic Mission's English-proficiency and domicile certificates
common_rejection_risks: Proposing a research area that is only adjacent to, rather than within, the notified priority areas
Arriving at the interview without the host university acceptance letter
Crossing the age ceiling (35 fresh, 40 in-service) on the last date for receipt, or being a fresh candidate whose Master's is more than two years old
Missing outside signatures: good-conduct certificate, deputation approval, medical fitness, and for overseas applicants the diplomatic mission certificates
Assuming tuition is included: US$2,000/month or INR 40,000/month does not cover fees at high-tuition universities, so an under-costed budget sinks the degree later
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Host institution tuition and fees, medical insurance and fitness tests, domestic travel within India for Indian fellows, the cost of furnishing the US$10,000 bank guarantee (rupee equivalent) and the Rs. 2,00,000 withheld from overseas fellows' first two installments, plus family and everyday living costs, especially in high-fee study destinations.
document_audit: Referee reports must follow the Council's prescribed format and one referee should preferably be your current supervisor; generic letters invite follow-up queries
Publications must be listed with NAAS score and journal ID (above NAAS rating 4.0) with copies attached, not just CV lines
The good-conduct certificate must come from the Competent Authority of the university last attended or your present employer, and in-service applicants also need deputation approval

Overseas applicants need the Indian Diplomatic Representative's certificate (domicile plus verified entries) and the mission-sealed English proficiency certificate, both of which take time to obtain from the mission
An acceptance letter that is missing, provisional or from outside the identified institution lists weakens the file at interview stage
alerts: The 2026 deadline of September 25, 2026 has passed; the scheme is annual, so monitor ICAR website notifications and national newspaper advertisements rather than relying on a standing deadline
Tenure is a strict three years with no extension, and if the degree is not completed within two years of its prescribed duration ICAR may recover the fellowship paid
Failing to register within one year of the award letter terminates the offer automatically with no separate communication

Indian fellows sign a US$10,000 bank guarantee and must return to India after the PhD (in-service fellows owe three years' service to the deputing institution); non-compliance triggers recovery with 10% overhead
First installment is released only after acceptance and the host admission letter, and later installments depend on six-monthly supervisor-certified progress reports
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch for the annual call in national newspapers and on the ICAR website, then e-mail the complete proforma plus certified enclosures to ADG (HRD) at adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com before the last date; shortlisting follows a weighted academic score, then a Selection Committee interview (in person, telephonic or by teleconference) where the host admission letter is produced.
